title: Exciton Alchemy: Chern Excitons from Trivial Bands
authors: Yoonseok Hwang, Henry Davenport, Frank Schindler
abstract: Exciton topology is commonly inherited from the topology of the underlying electronic bands. Recent theoretical work, however, has shown that the exciton Chern number can in general receive an additional contribution from the topology of the exciton envelope wave function, allowing, in principle, interaction-induced topological excitons even when the constituent electronic bands are topologically trivial. Here, we provide an explicit realization of this case by constructing a two-dimensional exciton model with topologically trivial conduction and valence bands that nevertheless hosts a Chern exciton diagnosed by inversion symmetry. Starting from a real-space limit of exponentially localized Wannier states for the conduction and valence bands, we identify the essential ingredients responsible for the emergent exciton topology and formulate a simple construction recipe. Our work demonstrates that interactions alone can generate nontrivial exciton topology, independent of the topology of the underlying electronic bands, and establishes a general framework for designing interaction-induced topological excitons.
summary: This paper presents a theoretical framework demonstrating that strong electron-hole interactions can induce non-trivial Chern topology in excitons even if the constituent electronic bands are topologically trivial. By constructing an explicit 2D model and analyzing its band structure using symmetry constraints and Wilson loops, the authors provide a general recipe for designing interaction-driven topological materials.
main_problem: To demonstrate that interaction-induced topological excitons (Chern excitons) can exist even when the underlying electronic bands are topologically trivial.
main_result: The authors constructed an explicit microscopic model showing that interactions alone can generate non-trivial exciton topology, independent of the band structure's intrinsic topology.
method: The study combines real-space modeling with symmetry analysis (inversion eigenvalues) and momentum-space diagnostics using Wilson loops to calculate the Chern number.
model_or_system: A two-dimensional exciton model is used, derived from exponentially localized Wannier states for conduction and valence bands. The system's Hamiltonian includes hopping terms and density-density interactions ($U$ terms).
key_observables: Chern exciton number ($C_{exc}$), Wilson loop spectra ($\arg W(p_y)$), and chiral edge states in ribbon geometry.
important_parameters: Interaction strengths ($U_0, U_x, U_y, V_x$) and the small electron-hole separation $\Delta$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on restricting the Hilbert space to the active conduction-valence subspace; some calculations use a coincident embedding approximation for simplification.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the unit cell geometry, the effect of interactions leading to band inversion (Fig. 1c), and confirm the topology via bulk spectra showing gaps and ribbon spectra exhibiting chiral edge states (Fig. 2d).
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the theoretical possibility of interaction-induced topology, constructing an explicit model using Wannier states, demonstrating band inversion via specific interactions ($V_x$), and finally confirming the non-trivial topology using momentum-space diagnostics like Wilson loops.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, controllable mechanism (interaction tuning) to engineer topological properties in excitons, which are neutral quasiparticles relevant for quantum light sources and optoelectronics.
